title: Optimizing Input Minimization in Kernel Fuzzing
problem: Input minimization in kernel fuzzing is computationally expensive, requiring repeated kernel executions to identify minimal crash-triggering inputs, creating a bottleneck in fuzzing campaigns.
motivation: Minimized inputs are critical for understanding bugs, improving crash reproducibility, and accelerating fuzzing throughput.
method: The paper likely employs algorithmic optimizations such as delta-debugging variants, binary search heuristics, or execution prediction to reduce minimization iterations. Techniques may include selective input section elimination, reuse of execution metadata across minimization steps, or parallelization of minimization trials.
key_novelty: Accelerated input minimization for kernel fuzzing through optimized search strategies or kernel-aware execution prediction.
contributions: Optimized algorithm for input minimization in kernel fuzzing
Evaluation demonstrating significant speedup in minimization time
Analysis of tradeoffs between minimization quality and performance
